title: Could It Happen Here? Hazira gas terminal release and fire, 2020
audience: HSE managers and advisers at the organisation's other sites
status: Learning purposes: not a statutory document. Draft learnings from a ProbeMatrix investigation export; validate them before adoption.

data_quality.text: Draft learnings from an unreviewed analysis: the export's Investigation Status is in_progress and no finding is marked as edited by a person, so this pack stays a draft, and cannot be shared outside the organisation, until the investigation is completed and reviewed.

bottom_line.text: The release came from a pressure-boundary seal fitted without a specification and put back into service without a test to design pressure: check whether your site carries the same two conditions.
Isolation took about 46 minutes, because the plan held no isolation criteria and the valves could be closed only by hand inside the vapour cloud: check your emergency plan and isolation valves next.

items.text: A self-assessment for each site. Results show coverage and conditions, never a ranking of sites.

The HSE lead at each site works through every self-check with the people who do the work, against the site's own records and plant. Look for the condition, not for a repeat of the event: the same condition can sit behind a different leak, a different valve or a different fire.

Record one answer for each self-check on the site's return: present, partly, absent or n/a. Add the site's response and the role of the person who assessed it. The organisation sets the date for returns.

items.condition: A pressure-boundary seal or gasket is replaced with a part that has no written specification, or with a substitute no one has approved.
items.evidence_to_check: For each pressure-boundary seal or gasket fitted in the last two years, a specification or an approved substitute is on file and matches the part that was bought.
items.look_in: Spares and purchase records, the stores catalogue and the maintenance history of older equipment

items.condition: Pressure-boundary work goes back into service without a test to design pressure, because no procedure requires one.
items.evidence_to_check: Recent seal, gasket or flange jobs on pressure equipment each have a test record that names the test type and pressure, and a return-to-service procedure requires it.
items.look_in: Work orders, test certificates and the procedure index

items.condition: A repair on a high-consequence pressure boundary rests on one person's judgement, with no independent check of the part, the method or the test.
items.evidence_to_check: Job plans for these repairs name a check of the part, a witnessed test and a close-out review, and the records show each was done.
items.look_in: Job plans, permits and inspection or witness-point records

items.condition: Repeat failures of the same component are repaired as routine each time, with no root-cause review or engineering look at why they recur.
items.evidence_to_check: The maintenance system can list the components repaired three or more times in two years, and each one has a root-cause review or an engineering decision on record.
items.look_in: The failure history in the maintenance management system and the reliability or engineering review log

items.condition: The management-of-change procedure exists on paper, but a different part, material or pipe route goes in without it.
items.evidence_to_check: The MOC register shows recent entries, and a sample of recent part or material substitutions each has an MOC record.
items.look_in: The MOC register, recent purchase substitutions and modification work orders

items.condition: The emergency plan names a major release but gives no criteria for when to isolate and no standing authority for the shift to order it.
items.evidence_to_check: For each major release scenario, the plan states the isolation trigger, the valves to close and which shift role may order isolation without waiting for a senior manager.
items.look_in: The on-site emergency plan, its checklists and the control-room standing orders

items.condition: When a release blocks access, the response plan still sends people to find the leak instead of switching to isolation from a safe place.
items.evidence_to_check: Emergency drills and the control-room decision aids include a release that blocks access, and drill records show the switch to remote or upstream isolation.
items.look_in: Drill reports, emergency scenario cards and the control-room console aids

items.condition: Emergency isolation valves can be closed only by hand at the valve, inside the area a release would make unreachable.
items.evidence_to_check: The list of emergency isolation valves shows for each whether it can be closed remotely, and the risk that a release denies access to it has been assessed.
items.look_in: The isolation valve list, the P&IDs and the site's risk assessment for releases

items.condition: Gas detectors only raise an alarm: they start no shutdown, isolation or protection, and their readings are not kept.
items.evidence_to_check: The fire and gas cause-and-effect chart shows which detectors trip a shutdown or start protection, and the control system stores detector history.
items.look_in: The fire and gas cause-and-effect chart, the control system configuration and the alarm history

items.condition: Damaged flameproof electrical equipment stays in service in a hazardous area, because electrical maintenance waits for breakdowns.
items.evidence_to_check: Each item of hazardous-area electrical equipment has its own inspection record within the inspection interval, and the defects found are closed out.
items.look_in: The hazardous-area equipment register, the electrical inspection records and a walk of the hazardous areas

items.condition: Control-room staff hold emergency duties with no defined qualification and no simulator or practised emergency training.
items.evidence_to_check: A control-room qualification is defined, and each person on the emergency roster has met it, with simulator or drill practice on record.
items.look_in: Training records, the competence framework and the control-room roster

items.text: The organisation brings the returns together into one view: for each learning, how many sites assessed it, and for each condition, how many sites found it present or partly. The view never ranks or scores a site. A site that finds a condition present has done what the assessment asks, and its response goes into its own action process.

limits: The self-checks are drawn from the Learnings Register's 11 priority-1 learnings, all transferable; the 14 priority-2 and priority-3 learnings are not here, and a site may add them.
Each condition is described from a desk review of the published enquiry report on the incident site. The pack says nothing about any other site until that site answers.
